prompt_context: Draft a Bail Application before the Magistrate / CJM under Section 480 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 (corresponding to Section 437 CrPC). DISTINCTION: Section 480 BNSS deals with bail by the trial court / magistrate; Section 483 BNSS deals with special powers of High Court / Sessions Court. The Magistrate's competence is limited — it cannot grant bail in offences punishable with death or imprisonment for life, unless certain conditions are met (under-18, woman, sick/infirm, no prima facie case after the court hears the prosecution). The application must: (1) establish particulars of FIR; (2) demonstrate offence is within Magistrate's bail competence; (3) apply the triple-test (flight risk, tampering, influence) — Sushila Aggarwal v. State (NCT of Delhi) (2020) 5 SCC 1; P. Chidambaram v. Directorate of Enforcement (2019) 9 SCC 24; (4) show clean antecedents or contextualise; (5) furnish undertakings. Cite BNS for offences (never IPC), BNSS for procedural provisions.
promptInstructions: Draft a Bail Application before the Magistrate under Section 480 BNSS, 2023 (successor to Section 437 CrPC).
Confirm at outset that the offence is within the Magistrate's bail competence under BNSS 480.
If offence is punishable with death / life imprisonment, the Magistrate's powers are restricted — flag whether applicant falls in special categories (woman / under-18 / sick / infirm).
Set out FIR particulars and circumstances of arrest.
Apply the triple-test: flight risk (no — give antecedents and roots), tampering with evidence (no — give reasons), influencing witnesses (no — distance from witnesses).
Cite Sushila Aggarwal v. State (NCT of Delhi) (2020) 5 SCC 1 on grant of bail principles.
Cite P. Chidambaram v. Directorate of Enforcement (2019) 9 SCC 24 on the triple test.
If charge sheet has been filed, mention that custody is no longer required for investigation.
Include undertakings: attend court on every date, not tamper with evidence, not leave jurisdiction.
Use BNS section numbers for offences (never IPC).
Do NOT generate the verification clause or advocate signature block — those are added programmatically.
